From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2027 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Post-demo: token volumes, target $/1M & CAC payback — internal calc (draft)

Jordan / team —

I ran a quick internal sensitivity table based on Emma’s numbers. Below are illustrative, high-level assumptions and outputs we can include in the customer note (call these "starter" figures; we should mark them as estimates until we agree on exact session counting and retention).

Assumptions used:
- Pilot MAU: 10,000 monthly active users
- Customer confirmation flow: 300 tokens / session, 1 session/user/month (light)
- Agent assist flow: 1,200 tokens / session, 0.2 sessions/user/month (agents trigger occasionally)
- Token mix initial: 75% customer confirmations, 25% agent assist (by session count)
- Inference cost (our backend run): raw GPU cost equivalent = $45 / 1M tokens (baseline unquantized); with quantization & batching potential: $25 (medium), $15 (optimized)
- Target gross margin target for Redwood on this segment: 40–55% (depends on value capture and support/SLAs)
- CAC target for Luma feature: we should show payback windows of 1, 3, 6 months to be realistic for enterprise pilot adoption

Outputs (illustrative):
- Estimated tokens/month: (10,000 MAU) * [0.75*300 + 0.25*1,200*0.2] = ~2.7M tokens/month
- Cost to Redwood (baseline): 2.7 * $45 = $121.5k / month
- Cost to Redwood (quantized medium): 2.7 * $25 = $67.5k / month
- Cost to Redwood (optimized): 2.7 * $15 = $40.5k / month

Suggested commercial starter bands (per 1M tokens):
- Pilot band (capped): $80 / 1k tokens => $80,000 / 1M tokens (this is a packaged pilot price that includes SLAs & onboarding support) — note: that is list pilot pricing, not ideal for long-term margins
- Standard consumption band: $30,000 – $45,000 / 1M tokens (maps to $30–45 per 1k tokens) depending on committed volume and reserved capacity
- Optimized (volume / committed): $18,000 – $25,000 / 1M tokens (if they commit to a 12mo reserved capacity and accept quantized models)

Mapping to $/feature (approx):
- Customer confirmation (~300 tokens): at $30,000 / 1M tokens => per-feature cost = 300 * ($30,000 / 1,000,000) = $9.00 / confirmation
- Agent assist (~1,200 tokens): at $30,000 / 1M => $36.00 / assist

CAC payback scenarios (example):
- If Luma charges $2 / confirmation and $50 / agent-assist (gross to them), with 10k MAU and conversion rates, we can show payback on their acquisition cost. We should build a 3-row table for 1m, 3m, 6m payback but for the note to customer keep two simple scenarios: conservative (3–6 months) and aggressive (1–3 months) depending on uptake.

Notes / next steps for customer-facing note: 
1) Present three $/1M bands with clear labels: Pilot (capped), Consumption, Committed/Optimized.
2) Show $/feature examples for both flows and one blended unit-econ line.
3) Include an appendix with technical options that reduce cost: 8-bit quantization, KV cache reuse, and per-route batching. Rishi — can you add a short blurb (2–3 lines) about expected latency/quality tradeoffs at each quant level so we can include it?

I’ll assemble a draft pricing note and send to Jordan for external.

—
Ben Carter
Head of Revenue Ops | Redwood Inference
